verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim is itself a simulation sandbox. Its docs describe training and evaluating perception and mobility stacks in simulation with software-in-the-loop or hardware-in-the-loop testing, plugging into existing testing and validation pipelines, and validating ROS 2 stacks in simulated worlds. Programmatic world loading, entity spawning and stepping, plus Docker for repeatable setups, let testing happen without involving real robots or live data. Missing for 10: explicit documentation framing isolation from production data or systems (it is only implied by simulation), and independent hands-on corroboration of sandbox-style test workflows.
